subject: docs/litmus/parts/{a,b,c,d}.json
method: Worked the 21 findings in id order. Read nothing in the repository outside the files the brief names, so every rewrite is still a reflection on PASS.md Part B and the web rather than on anything this repository built. Duplicated B3/B4 pairs were resolved by rewriting the concern side to ask what only a concern can ask - whether the guarantee rides on every unit of work through every entry unrequested - never by dropping a section below the frame's minimum of four questions and four angles including depth and usage. Missing angles were added as new questions at the section's next id. Anchors that readmitted what they forbade were rewritten so aligned and misaligned exclude each other. Three future_state fields whose own gaps disclaimed their load-bearing sentence were re-marked proposed with the synthesis named inside the text. The date conflict was settled by a web search recorded as a new research record in each affected part's research file, and both texts were corrected against it.

applied.change: concern-telemetry rewritten so it no longer restates the capability section. q2 narrowed to the after-the-fact join where trace context never survived (queue, restart, hand-off to a party that never saw it). q3 replaced: it now asks whether the attributes the other guarantees need - actor and delegation chain, tenant, entry, policy outcome, ceiling and consumption - are stamped by the platform onto metrics and logs as well as spans, leaving the convention-version question to the capability section alone. q4 replaced with the caller-side question only the concern can ask: what a caller must do to be observable at each entry and whether it can suppress, resample or over-emit beyond the guarantee. q5 replaced: backend replaceability is left to the capability section, and the slot now asks whether instrumentation attaches at the interface so an implementation added tomorrow with no telemetry code is observed identically.

concern-provenance q2 and q3 replaced. q2 now asks whether an artifact whose attestation is missing or fails verification is refused by the platform at the point of consumption or promotion, which was previously buried as the second half of q6. q3 now asks for coverage that can be counted: a reconciliation of artifacts produced against records emitted, plus an attempt to produce an artifact through a component carrying no attestation code. Independent verification and predicate content stay with the capability section.

concern-errors q2, q3 and q6 replaced so the registry, transport-mapping and caller-retry questions live only in the capability section. q2 now asks whether the platform's own stops - refusal, ceiling exceeded, cancellation, validation rejection, isolation kill - each arrive as a distinct typed failure rather than a silence. q3 now asks whether a failure where nobody is waiting (schedule fire, redelivered event, spawned sub-unit) is still constructed, recorded and retrievable. q6 now asks whether the typed failure is the platform's own currency for recovery, with nothing inside it recovering by reading prose or handing the message to a model.

Added state-persistence-q7, a guarantees question asking which cross-cutting guarantees attach at the moment of an append - actor, delegation chain, correlation, the decision that admitted the write - with evidence being one full append record, the place those fields are stamped, and two bypass attempts (a component that supplies none of them, and a direct write to the underlying store). Both depth questions were kept, since the frame allows up to eight questions. The future_state gained a sentence requiring every append to carry the guarantees.

concern-policy q2, q3 and q5 replaced; the decision record, the data-not-conditionals test and the second engine stay with the capability section. q2 now asks what a sub-unit spawned mid-run is decided against (actor, delegation chain, remaining ceiling at that moment). q3 now asks whether an allow has a stated scope and lifetime and is re-evaluated on resume after a pause, queue or restart. q5 now asks whether enforcement is reached by construction, so an adapter added tomorrow with no policy code still cannot execute an undecided action.

concern-idempotency q1 replaced by the opt-out question: whether any flag, omitted field, trusted path or direct implementation call runs a unit unclaimed. The derivation-when-no-key content moved into q4, the usage question, which also keeps tenant scoping and the same work arriving by two doors. q5 replaced (the capability section owns the claim-store boundary) with a depth question on whether the units the platform generates for itself - a scheduled retry, a compensation, a spawned sub-unit, a step resumed after a crash - are keyed from the parent and the step so a restart does not repeat them.

concern-identity q5 narrowed to the revocation-in-flight half and extended to ask whether the withdrawal is recorded against the unit it stopped; the credential-lifetime half is left to the capability section. q2 sharpened so it is unambiguously about the stored action record rather than the presented credential, and asks whether the ordered chain is still recoverable from the record after the credentials have expired.

Added scheduling-q7, a direction question asking whether a schedule is durable inspectable state the platform owns rather than host configuration or an in-process timer, and whether a fleet declares its overlap policy and spreads its fires; evidence is the stored schedule set, the recorded last and next fire, and the fire-time distribution across many schedules sharing one rule. Jitter is now scoreable.

concern-provenance-q6 anchor no longer readmits what it forbids: 'or a documented equivalent with stated rotation' is deleted and replaced by the property - the signing credential is issued for that signing, expires, and is not recoverable from the build afterwards. The misaligned anchor now says a long-lived key with the build is misaligned whatever the rotation paperwork says.

The unfalsifiable escape is gone with the question: concern-policy-q5's 'or every difference is written down as a known divergence' was removed when the question was replaced by the enforcement-by-construction question under R66-005. Second-engine equivalence now sits only in the capability section, where its anchor carries no written-down escape.

Both anchors now cap a document at 'exists'. telemetry-q6 asks for one convention change actually absorbed, with signals before, during and after, and states that a written statement with no transition exercised is exists rather than aligned. model-access-q6 asks for the change set of a second wire family actually added, with the same explicit cap.

All three future_state fields whose own gap disclaimed their load-bearing sentence are now origin proposed, with the word proposed in the text and the synthesised clause named inside it: scheduling ('as this section proposes rather than sources' on the replay identity derived from schedule and nominal fire time), concern-budget ('proposed here as a consequence of the ceiling riding on the unit, not as a sourced convention' on carry-over across a restart), and state-persistence ('as this section proposes rather than sources' on the three-operation read surface). The now-unused quote field was dropped from each.

Settled by web search rather than by picking a side. Two new research records, X-litmus-c-025 and X-litmus-b-026, carry a snippet stating that the agent messaging specification reached v1.0 on 12 March 2026 and that this release carried signed agent cards, with 9 April 2026 being the 150-organisation adoption announcement. concern-identity's standard.why and direction were corrected from 'January 2026' to the 12 March 2026 release, which is inside the window and is now said to be; work-intake's standard.why and direction were corrected from 'reached v1.0 in April 2026' to the same release date with the April announcement named for what it is. The losing records are left in place and the new records are cited alongside them.

concern-idempotency-q2's anchors and the section's future_state are now split by who owns the resource: where the platform owns the effect, the resource must refuse the stale holder's lower token; where the effect lands on a resource the platform cannot fence, the effect must be made through a keyed operation whose stored outcome the stale holder reads before writing. Having no answer at all for foreign effects is what the misaligned anchor now catches.

Added concern-budget-q7, a boundary question that makes the section's stated exit scoreable: is the unit of measure a declared mapping applied at one recording point, and can the measurement source be replaced without moving any enforcement point; evidence is the mapping site, the list of enforcement points, and the change set for a source swap with the same run terminating at the same place before and after. An exit described but never exercised is named as misaligned.

capability-packaging's direction restated around what actually moved inside the window - roughly 40 conformant products by June 2026, the registry scale as of May 2026 and the vulnerability scan - with the December 2025 publication of the specification kept as context and explicitly placed before the window opened.

Both judgements replaced by observables. isolation-q2 now requires each field that departs from the default to be traceable to a field in the unit's own declaration, rather than 'justified'. capability-packaging-q1 now requires the description to be the text a selector actually matches on, shown by a selection that changed when the description changed, and its evidence asks for that repeated selection.

concern-policy-q6 now distinguishes the deterministic check over the declared action and its arguments from a probabilistic judgement of the model's output: the question names the distinction, the aligned anchor says argument scanning feeds the decision input rather than standing in for the decision, and the misaligned anchor is scoped to the probabilistic judgement. The section's direction quote is left as it is, since the question no longer reads as forbidding what the quote describes.

scheduling's future_state now requires what no shipped scheduler gives: the recurrence together with its missed-fire and catch-up bound, its overlap policy and its jitter declared in one portable record that moves between runners intact, so none of it is inherited from a particular runner's feature set - which is what the boundary question already presumed.

Added document-validation-q7, a depth question asking whether each boundary schema is versioned in its own right, separately from the dialect, and what a document written to the previous version receives once the schema changes; evidence is one schema change with both version identifiers and the failure object produced for a document valid under the old version.

concern-errors-q1's evidence now points at what distinguishes it from the capability question: the single place the failure object is constructed and the path every boundary takes to it, plus a failure raised through a component that contains no error-handling code of its own. The anchors were rewritten to match.

summary: All 21 findings applied, none declined. The six B3/B4 pairs the review flagged are now written so each side asks what the other does not: the concern sections ask whether the guarantee rides unrequested on every unit through every entry, reaches units nobody is waiting for, survives an adapter added with no code for it, and cannot be declined; the capability sections keep the registry, the second engine, the independent verifier, backend replaceability and transport mapping. Four sections gained a question (state-persistence a guarantees question, scheduling a direction question, concern-budget a boundary question, document-validation a schema-versioning question), taking the questionnaire from 140 to 144. Three future_state fields that claimed to be sourced while their own gaps disclaimed them are now proposed with the synthesis named in the text. The A2A date conflict was settled by search: v1.0 on 12 March 2026, inside the window, with two new research records and both texts corrected. Every part and the full run check at 0 errors.
